summary.headline: Ola Electric Q4 FY26 consolidated gross margin rose to 38.5% and first positive operating cash flow (Rs 91 crore CFO), but revenue was low on depressed deliveries.
summary.overview: Management framed Q4 FY26 as a reset quarter: gross margin reached 38.5% (33.5% excluding PLI) versus 13.7% a year earlier, and consolidated OpEx including leases fell to Rs 428 crore from Rs 844 crore. Revenue was weak because deliveries were depressed by internal service and operations fixes, with FY26 consolidated revenue at Rs 2,253 crore on 173,794 deliveries. Management says registrations have recovered for three months, orders are running ahead of registrations, and Q1 FY27 guidance is 40,000-45,000 orders and Rs 500-550 crore revenue. The Gigafactory's first 3 GWh is in ramp-up with the remaining 3.5 GWh slated for June, and the company is pushing Shakti and Roadster bike growth.

segments.name: Auto (electric two-wheelers)
segments.commentary: Generates 100% of revenue today; Auto CFO Rs 213 crore and FCF Rs 173 crore in Q4 FY26. Roadster bikes are about 15% of April gross orders, with Ola holding about 50% share of electric motorcycles.

segments.name: Cell (Gigafactory)
segments.commentary: 2.5 GWh operational, with 6 GWh installation largely complete; commercialisation of the full 6 GWh expected by end of Q1 FY27. Still in investment phase, with cell CapEx for 6 GWh essentially done apart from payouts in Q1-Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Shakti / Mahashakti (ESS)
segments.commentary: Shakti launched last quarter and supply-constrained because cells are prioritised for Auto; Mahashakti grid storage on a prismatic LFP platform is in product development with details due over the next couple of quarters.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27: 40,000-45,000 orders and consolidated revenue of Rs 500-550 crore, nearly double Q4 level.
Adjusted operating EBITDA breakeven at about 20,000-25,000 units per month on consolidated basis, subject to pricing mix and commodity conditions.
Consolidated OpEx to move toward about Rs 350 crore, with management also citing Rs 300-350 crore next quarter and Rs 100-120 crore per month in coming quarters.
Auto expected to reach adjusted operating EBITDA and cash flow positivity through FY27.
Operating cash burn of Rs 300-500 crore over FY27 as volumes rise; positive after 20,000-25,000 orders per month. Debt repayments of Rs 400+ crore in FY27.

Gigafactory: about 2+ GWh output by September 2026; FY27 allocation about 2 GWh captive, 1+ GWh external auto sales, remainder for Shakti/Mahashakti. Full vehicle portfolio to move to own cells by September 2026.
Maintenance CapEx for Auto about Rs 50 crore per year; R&D to be mid-single-digit % of revenue as revenue ramps.
Expansion from 6 GWh to 20 GWh and prismatic capacity contingent on raising capital at cell subsidiary level, planned this financial year.
capex_capacity: Auto capacity of up to 1 million units per year already built; no meaningful incremental CapEx needed to scale.
Gigafactory: 2.5 GWh operational; 3 GWh commissioned and ramping; remaining 3.5 GWh to be completed in June 2026 after container delays linked to the Iran war.
Combined asset base can support about Rs 15,000-20,000 crore annual revenue across Auto and Cell without meaningful incremental CapEx.
Expansion beyond 6 GWh to 20 GWh, and prismatic cell capacity, to be funded by separate capital raise at cell subsidiary.
demand_pricing: Registrations: about 10,000 in March, 12,000 in April (up 20% MoM while the broader e-2W industry fell over 22%), and May trending to 14,000-15,000; management expects 17,000-18,000 units per month from rebound, then 20,000-22,000 over the next quarter.
Average ASP about Rs 1.4 lakh; gross profit about Rs 50,000 per vehicle. Q4 ASP was lowered by a revenue-recognition change for extended warranty packages, a one-time hit of about Rs 20-30 crore.
Company runs very low free inventory of 3-4 days and has an auto backlog; no dealer model, so orders, registrations and deliveries are reported separately.
Own 4680 cells cheaper than imported cells on BOM even at low volume; expected 10-15% advantage at 6 GWh including overheads.
Brand recall and NPS are cited as above industry averages; no TV or print advertising at present, though some advertising may come in coming months.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 revenue not reflect strong March sales and the orders data?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said March registrations were about 10,000 and April about 12,000, with May trending 14,000-15,000; Q4 revenue was low because operations were being fixed and volumes restarted only mid-March, with production backlog spilling into Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the bridge from current volumes to the 20,000 units/month breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Rebound should reach about 17,000-18,000 units per month including about 15% bikes; better service stability and inventory availability could take volumes to 20,000-22,000 over the next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Advantage of own cells versus imported cells?
qa_highlights.answer: Own cells are already cheaper on pure BOM even at low volumes; at 6 GWh with overheads the advantage is expected to be 10-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Why not advertise in print media, and is the Rs 2,000 crore cell monetisation progressing?
qa_highlights.answer: Company prefers word-of-mouth and does not do TV or IPL sponsorship; may advertise in coming months. Cell monetisation requires a subsidiary-level capital raise; management has inbound PE interest but gave no timing beyond 'in due course'.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the one-time ASP change and will prior quarters be restated?
qa_highlights.answer: Extended warranty packages moved from upfront to deferred revenue recognition after discussion with auditors, a Rs 20-30 crore impact already baked into published numbers; no restatement of prior quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 CapEx, R&D and cash burn outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Auto maintenance CapEx about Rs 50 crore per year, PPE CapEx below Rs 50 crore; cell CapEx for 6 GWh essentially complete; R&D mid-single-digit % of revenue; operating cash burn Rs 300-500 crore in FY27, turning positive after 20,000-25,000 orders per month.

qa_highlights.question: Status of solid-state and sodium-ion cell technologies?
qa_highlights.answer: Both are at lab scale; focus is on ramping 46-series NMC, with an LFP cell to start ramping in the factory next quarter; solid-state and sodium to be commercialised as the industry matures.

qa_highlights.question: Why are service issues linked to parts unavailability, and why NMC for Shakti?
qa_highlights.answer: Parts were not stocked at service centres and procurement was reactive (20-30 day fulfilment); now stocked locally and procured on forecasts. Shakti uses NMC today and will move to LFP next quarter; Shakti ramp is slower because NMC 46-series goes to Auto.

risks_watch: Volume recovery must reach 20,000-25,000 units per month for adjusted EBITDA breakeven; Q1 FY27 guidance is 40,000-45,000 orders versus registrations trending at 14,000-15,000 in May.
Gigafactory ramp: 3 GWh still ramping, 3.5 GWh due in June, and 2+ GWh output targeted by September; supply-chain localisation and commodity (lithium upcycle) pressures.
Funding dependence: 20 GWh expansion and prismatic capacity require a subsidiary capital raise with no firm timeline; net debt about Rs 950 crore and Rs 400+ crore repayments in FY27.
Service and parts supply chain still incomplete; store experience described as improved but not yet at earlier levels.
Bike EV and Roadster ramp and new product launches (Mahashakti, LFP Shakti) depend on supply and timing; an Analyst Day is planned in one to two months.
Margin sustainability: management flagged short-term commodity pressure and aggressive growth investment in the last month or two.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on margins, cash flow and demand recovery, with numbers given for most claims. Cautious and less specific on the cell monetisation, timelines for the 20 GWh expansion, and service execution, where answers were often deferred to later quarters.
key_quotes: Q4 was the first operating cash flow positive quarter.
And for our Auto business, there is no more CapEx needed as we scale up.
So, by end of next quarter, which is September, we expect our Gigafactory to be producing about 2+ GWh already.
We don't plan to have any dealerships in our auto business, we believe our strategy is correct.

growth.why: Q1 FY27 guidance of Rs 500-550 crore revenue (nearly double Q4) and 40,000-45,000 orders, backed by a free inventory of 3-4 days, an auto backlog, and registrations rising from about 10,000 in March to 12,000 in April, with 3 GWh already ramping and 3.5 GWh due in June, but revenue and quarterly growth % were not stated.
